# Method input isolation policy

**Allowlist version:** `DA01_METHOD_INPUTS_V1`

**Bundle rule:** include only files generated by `tooling.inputs`; never export a
whole checkout and then delete known secret files.

## Per-method permissions

| Input | B0 | B1 | P |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frozen before/target application Python source at explicit SHAs | yes | yes | yes |
| Sanitized structural observations and target module manifest facts | yes | yes | yes |
| A0 fitness config, representation catalog, and original evaluator | unchanged | yes | yes |
| Full general obligation registry | assessment | yes | yes |
| Shared generic evaluator capability inventory | no | yes | yes |
| A0 traceability as an impact-analysis model | no | no | yes |
| DA01 `scenario.yaml`, full scenario README, validation report | no | no | no |
| Ground truth, expected operations, affected targets, new-obligation answers | no | no | no |
| Engineering acceptance scripts, private scorer/reference rules | no | no | no |
| Git metadata/history/remotes and other method outputs | no | no | no |

The exporter reads only pinned Git blobs for the allowlisted files and emits a
new bundle outside the checkout. It records every included relative path, role,
size, and exact-byte SHA-256. It rejects symlinks, unknown files, forbidden path
components, and bundle-manifest mismatches. The generated architecture
observations contain structural source facts, not scenario labels or fitness
decisions.

## Execution boundary

The Docker runner requires a digest-pinned runtime image. It mounts only
`/input` read-only and `/output` read-write, uses a non-root UID, a read-only
container root, no network, no added capabilities, and bounded process/memory/CPU
resources. It does not inherit host environment variables or mount the checkout,
`.git`, ground truth, scorer, or another method output. Commands are argument
arrays, never shell strings. Missing Docker or an invalid image digest is a hard
isolation error, not permission to fall back to an ordinary subprocess.

These controls reduce file, history, remote, and network access through the
provided runner. They do not certify arbitrary host/container-runtime compromise;
record the runtime image digest and Docker version as provenance.

## Negative probes

Synthetic probes attempt to read a private absolute ground-truth path, find Git
history, traverse another method's output, write into read-only inputs, and open
a network connection. The probe passes only when each attempt is denied or the
path is absent. A regression sentinel placed in a forbidden source file must not
appear in any allowlisted bundle file or manifest.
